read.thesis: Amex beat and raised FY26 EPS to $18.30-$18.60 GAAP ($17.60-$17.90 adjusted) on 9% Q3 revenue growth, but the lift is mostly GBTG gain and a reserve release, not supply-side evidence.

triggers.label: FY26 adj EPS guide raised to $17.60-$17.90
triggers.quote: we are raising our full-year EPS guidance to between $18.30 and $18.60 ($17.60-$17.90 adjusted)

triggers.label: Q3 provisions fell on reserve release
triggers.quote: The decrease reflected a reserve release during the quarter compared to a reserve build in the prior year, partially offset by higher net write-offs.

guidance.quote: we are raising our full-year EPS guidance to between $18.30 and $18.60 ($17.60-$17.90 adjusted)
we're on track to deliver another year of 10 percent revenue growth

red_flags.label: Reported EPS flattered by one-off GBTG gain
red_flags.quote: which excludes the $982 million pre-tax gain ($751 million after-tax) from the previously-announced sale

red_flags.label: Legal reserves increase
red_flags.quote: partially offset by an increase in legal reserves for previously-disclosed matters

red_flags.label: Tax rate drop from discrete items
red_flags.quote: primarily reflecting discrete tax benefits in the current year related to the resolution of certain prior-period tax items
